newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures close down, fresh contract lows hit.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures close down, fresh contract lows hit.

text.p: Frozen concentrated orange juice futures resumed their downtrend, hitting fresh life of contract lows in the front five months and settling sharply weaker.

Traders said early speculative selling set off stops just below 75.00 cents in May and attracted fund selling. Analysts expect May to find support between 72.00 and 70.00 cents with an ultimate downside objective of 66.50 cents.
The spot month closed down 2.10 cents at 72.80 cents per lb, having ranged from 76.00 to 72.60 cents, a new contract low. The back months finished 2.25 to 1.65 weaker.
Volume was estimated at 2,500 lots compared to Monday's official 1,980 lots.

While market analysts blamed today's losses on technicals, they said several bearish fundamental factors continue to weigh on the market. "Brazil keeps coming in with huge numbers and we're dealing with oversupply and no demand," an analyst said.

The U.S. Department of Agriculture will release its monthly estimates of the Florida crop on Friday. The market expects the box count to remain unchanged at 222 million 90-lb boxes, and yields to rise slightly from 1.54 gallons per box.
Open interest in May fell 866 lots to 12,498 lots, as of Monday's close.
